# Duck Initiative

> Duck Initiative is a small studio making add-ons for Blender. Its add-ons are sold under the label Waddle by Duck Initiative. The first one is Polygraph for Blender, which shows the vertex count a game engine will really load, checks it against a platform budget, and lists what to cut first.

Key facts:

- The full name is Polygraph for Blender, by Waddle by Duck Initiative. It is a Blender add-on and is not related to other software called PolyGraph.
- Polygraph 1.0 comes out on December 8, 2026. It runs on Blender 4.2 and later, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Blender counts the vertices it stores. glTF, Unity and Unreal Engine count them after splitting every UV seam and sharp edge. The default cube is 8 vertices in Blender and 24 in any engine. Polygraph counts the way each engine imports.
- Editions: Free; Pro for one person, $19; Studio for a team of five, $249. Pro and Studio go to $25 and $329 on January 12, 2027, when 2.0 comes out. 2.0 is free for everyone who owns 1.x.
- Free is on extensions.blender.org and Gumroad. Pro and Studio are on Superhive and Gumroad.
- 32 budgets ship with Pro and Studio and 5 with Free (Meta Quest, VRChat, Roblox, Fortnite UEFN, visionOS and more). 26 of them cite the page their limits come from. There are 21 mesh checks in every edition.
- Every edition is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later and can be used for paid work. There is no account and no licence key, and Polygraph works offline.
- Polygraph does not decimate or retopologise meshes, and it does not run inside Unity or Unreal.
- More add-ons are being made: Dancefloor, Abandonify and Proxyforge. None has a release date yet.

## Common questions

- **Why does Unity, Unreal or glTF show more vertices than Blender?** Blender stores one vertex for each corner position. A game engine needs one for every different normal, UV and colour that meets at a corner, so it splits vertices along UV seams, sharp edges and flat-shaded faces. The default cube is 8 vertices in Blender and 24 in any engine.
- **How can I see the engine's vertex count without exporting?** Polygraph shows it in the Polygraph tab of the 3D Viewport's Sidebar, counted the way glTF, Unity or Unreal Engine (Nanite off) imports, and the Active Object panel breaks the count down by cause. Engine counts are in every edition, Free included.
- **When does a mesh need 32-bit indices?** Past 65,535 engine vertices. Polygraph flags it, because some mobile targets don't like it.
- **How many triangles can a VRChat avatar have?** PC: 32,000 for Excellent and 70,000 for Good, Medium and Poor. Mobile: 7,500 Excellent, 10,000 Good, 15,000 Medium, 20,000 Poor. Bones, material slots, skinned meshes and texture memory are ranked too. Source: creators.vrchat.com, checked November 16, 2026.
- **What is the triangle budget on Meta Quest?** Per frame, 750k to 1M triangles on Quest 2 and Pro, 1.3M to 1.8M on Quest 3 and 3S. For a medium simulation, 200 to 300 draw calls on Quest 2 and Pro, 400 to 600 on Quest 3 and 3S. Source: developers.meta.com.
- **What is the Roblox triangle limit?** 20,000 triangles per mesh, and 4,000 for a rigid accessory. Source: create.roblox.com.
- **What are Fortnite UEFN prop budgets?** Epic's LOD0 targets are 2,500 triangles for a large prop, 900 for a medium one and 400 for a small one, and its validator warns past 30,000 vertices in a mesh. Source: dev.epicgames.com.
- **What about Apple Vision Pro?** visionOS: under 500,000 triangles and 500 draw calls in a Full Space, under 250,000 and 250 in the Shared Space. Source: developer.apple.com.
- **Does Polygraph reduce the polycount for me?** No. It doesn't decimate or retopologise. Where to Cut lists the changes that would save the most, and What If (Pro) shows what a change would save before you make it.
- **Which Blender versions does it support?** Blender 4.2 and later, on Windows, macOS and Linux.

All 32 budgets, each with its limits and the page they come from: [Budgets](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/#budgets).

## Polygraph

- [Polygraph guide](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/): installing it, every panel, engine counts, the 32 budgets and their sources, the 21 mesh checks, Where to Cut, What If, reports, the command line check and the Python API.
- [Editions compared](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/#editions): what Free, Pro and Studio each include, feature by feature.
- [Licence and terms](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/license/): the GPL code, what a purchase covers, how seats are counted, updates and the 2.0 upgrade.
- [Refunds](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/refunds/): 30 days from purchase; what is covered and how to ask.
- [Press kit](https://duckinitiative.com/polygraph/press/): the short description, a fact table, screenshots, clips and logos, free to use in coverage.
